notes: Fifth check batch (2026-10-31-check-5): four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) and no Opus run, all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (each transcript's assistant messages name only that model), uncommitted true over head 74112b4 and one skill_hash (1fdf0c9b); haiku-1 was shown 83 skills, the other three 209. Every transcript contains the new text ("when that call does not return") and the earlier markers ("A `for` reads the same way", "Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance", "a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field", "is a tail call, not a second step", "Keyword.fetch!"), so the runs read the current rules. Reads: all four SKILL.md only, so Expected reads is met. In the scratch folder all four files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.3). Doctests: haiku-1 1 of 1, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 3 of 3, sonnet-2 3 of 3.

Changed rules: one of the ten graded rules changed. git diff 74112b4 -- idiomatic-elixir/ adds to "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function" the clause "when that call does not return `{:ok, value}`, the `case` goes in a small private function". That rule is graded against the current text, but the new clause decides no verdict here: no run writes a one-step with or a case inside a with body, and every with body only builds a struct. The other nine rules are unchanged and are held to the 2026-10-31-b standard.

Closest calls. Match every expected shape: sonnet-2's line 142, defp parse_data(_payment_type, data), do: parse_payment(data), is violated, the same line 2026-10-31 graded violated in skill-sonnet-1; sonnet-1 here names both payment atoms in a guard (line 125). All four parse/1 heads have no is_binary(type) guard, so a non-string type reaches {:unsupported_event, type}; kept in checks, as 2026-10-31-b kept the same shape (counted, Haiku and Sonnet would be violated). Comments: haiku-1 lines 93-94 and haiku-2 lines 91-92 say "Each known string gets its own clause" (haiku-2 "Each known name gets its own clause"), which alone restates the code, but each comment goes on to the reason for the clauses, a sender growing the atom table, which the code cannot show; held clean as 2026-10-22-d held comments that give a reason, unlike 2026-10-31's skill-haiku-1 line 105, which gave none. Read required keys: haiku-1 lines 123-124 and haiku-2 lines 118-119 read customer_email and failure_reason with brackets; both fields are outside @enforce_keys and typed String.t() | nil, so optional, and neither is checked for nil, as 2026-10-31-b held skill-haiku-1's data["failure_reason"]. The `->` rule: haiku-2 line 143 is exactly 70 characters after the indentation, held clean as the 2026-10-31 grades held 70. Naming: sonnet-2 lines 115-117 rebind type and data to parsed values, allowed as before, and its map argument in the readers is not counted, as 2026-10-21-check-2 did not. Outside the list: sonnet-1's {:ok, / %Payment{...}} (lines 137-144) is a return value, not a call argument, as 2026-10-22-c held, so not counted under Build a multi-line argument; haiku-1's parse_data/2 (lines 109-113) and sonnet-1's (lines 125-129) mix a block with a do: clause, not counted because the block's body does not fit on the head's line, as the 2026-10-31 grades held; haiku-2's lines 105-106 are a head mix format breaks after a long guard with do: on the next line, the wrap the do: rule keeps; sonnet-2's line 114 wraps id in a one-key map to reuse string_field/2, which no rule covers.

Probe of 29 payloads (known types, a refund with amount and currency, unknown type, non-string and missing type, missing, nil, string and negative amount, missing and nil currency, missing and integer customer_email, missing payment_id, missing and integer failure_reason, missing refund fields, a string refund amount, string and out-of-range created, missing and non-string id, missing and list data, a string and a nil payload), run in the scratch folder against each compiled file; nothing raises. In all four: payment.succeeded, payment.failed and refund.created parse; an unknown type gives {:unsupported_event, "invoice.paid"}; a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, not unsupported; a nil or string amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}; refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field; an out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}; a payload missing type, id or data, list data or a non-map payload gives :invalid_payload; "type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123}. Differences: a negative amount is accepted only by haiku-1, whose type is integer(); a string created gives :invalid_payload in haiku-2 (its guard reads created) and {:invalid_field, "created"} in the others; "id" => 5 gives {:invalid_field, "id"} in sonnet-2 and :invalid_payload in the others; an integer customer_email or failure_reason is accepted by haiku-1 and haiku-2, rejected by naming the field in the two Sonnet runs; a string refund amount is rejected only by sonnet-2, whose Refund carries amount.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-31-b at 74112b4): Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-2's catch-all); Comments moves from Sonnet violated to clean (no wrong timestamp, all six Sonnet doctests pass). Every other rule stays clean in both tiers. Neither move follows from a text change, since the one changed clause decides nothing in this case; with two runs per tier they are differences between runs.
